bounds.note: both counting bounds are reported on every target, not only where one of them fires: the layer capacity `Delta * floor(V/2)` and the matching bound `ceil(|E| / nu)` with `nu` a maximum matching. Neither refutes `Delta` on a class-1 graph, which is what makes their silence on these targets a result rather than an unused test

timing.why: a single wall clock at 400-900 qubits moves by tens of percent between runs on a loaded host, which is the size of the differences read off these columns; each phase is therefore timed three times on the same rebuilt circuit and the row quotes the median, with all three samples recorded beside it so the statistic is recomputable and the spread it hid is visible

limitations: the construction space is a grammar of named wireings (chain, star, balanced binary tree, seeded random tree, ring), not a general synthesiser: the engine selects among constructions it knows how to build, and it cannot invent a topology that is not in the grammar
two targets are specified (GHZ and a ring graph state); a third would need its own construction family, so 'synthesis from a specification' is demonstrated, not generalised

the ranking is (depth, operations, max_edge_span) and the frontier is reported instead of a single winner, because depth and connectivity trade off; the ordering is a stated preference, not a measurement of quality
non-Clifford synthesis (Experiment C) is not implemented: the dense specification referee can decide such a circuit up to 10 qubits, but no search proposes one
wall clock is one host and one process, and the 1,000-qubit rows are dominated by circuit construction rather than by the referee

Experiment D's mapped depth is a routing bound, not a floor: the lookahead router improves every routed row in this record and a better one -- an initial-placement search, or a router that reorders commuting gates -- would improve it again; neither router is optimal

the lookahead's window is eight two-qubit gates and its tie-break order is a choice, not a measurement: it scores future wire distance and schedules swaps by earliest free layer, and a different window or scoring would move the numbers, which is why both routers are reported row by row
neither router reorders gates: the program order is routed as written, so commuting gates are never scheduled past each other even where a reordering would shorten the routing

the lookahead is a heuristic, not a theorem of non-degradation: at small widths (a 9-qubit balanced tree on a line) it has been measured to route two layers deeper than greedy, so the 100-qubit rows are the evidence and they do not promise the same ordering everywhere

the two-qubit counts are reported in three bases and none of them is a device measurement: abstract operations count a SWAP as one instruction, native entanglers assume the declared basis (one per SWAP here, i.e. a native SWAP), and CNOT-equivalent charges three CNOTs per SWAP. A CNOT-only backend therefore sees the third column, which for the greedy 100-qubit lattice tree is 3,381 rather than 1,193

mapped_depth is the total depth including the restore ladder, and depth_before_restore is the circuit before that ladder is appended; restore_depth_cost is the difference, reported so neither number can be mistaken for the other. No depth is decomposed into a native gate basis

Experiment D includes the swap ladder that restores the wire permutation (shown separately as depth_before_restore and restore_swap_gates): a compiler that tracks its final layout can absorb that cost, and the verifiable circuit cannot
the router assumes every node holds a qubit and every edge is one equally cheap two-qubit interaction; there is no device calibration, no error rate and no classical control cost in these numbers
referee agreement is demonstrated only where both tiers can run -- Clifford constructions up to 10 qubits -- and says nothing about a non-Clifford circuit, which only the dense tier can decide

the 400- and 900-qubit agreement rows pair this package's stabilizer tier with Stim, not with the dense tier, which refuses above 10 qubits and whose refusal is recorded as a row at each width. Stim decides the prepared state only, is Clifford-only, and reaches the circuit through this package's IR, so a shared translation bug would fool both referees. A missing Stim is UNAVAILABLE and the rows record no agreement rather than a weaker one, and a comparative disagreement stops the write instead of being recorded

Experiment E's edge chromatic number is proved, not asserted, by an argument that carries a budget: the Delta-colouring search is complete, so a colouring it finds is minimal by the degree bound and a refutation of Delta proves the graph class 2 (then Delta + 1 is minimal by Vizing). Delta is refuted either by layer capacity -- more edges than Delta layers of floor(V/2) can hold, which is what decides the odd complete graphs -- or by exhausting the search space. Deciding the Delta case is NP-complete, so a search that only hits its node budget decides nothing: it reports the constructed Delta + 1 colouring (at most one layer above the minimum by Vizing) marked optimal=False rather than claiming a minimum

the minimum schedule saves nothing on the four Experiment E targets: the greedy peel already attained Delta on all of them, so the record reports 0 layers saved there and 12 on the class-2 graphs, where the peel's 15 layers on K9 and K11 are proved down to 9 and 11

the cluster target is the graph state of a square lattice with qubits on its vertices, not the surface-code cluster whose qubits sit on the edges of a lattice, and no error-correction property is claimed for it

the per-schedule wall clock is one run in this process on this host (the host is recorded with the dense-tier probe): synthesis is the time to build the circuit from the specification and verification is the time for the stabilizer referee to decide it, both measured on a circuit rebuilt from the same family and target and checked against the row's SHA-256. It is a measurement of this Python implementation on this machine, not a benchmark against another engine and not a hardware estimate. Both phases are timed on a rebuild in a warm process -- the same family has already been built and decided once for the outcome and the ranking -- so they are not cold-start numbers, and they move by tens of percent between runs under load

the irregular targets are seeded random spanning trees with extra edges: reproducible and without regular structure, but not adversarial, and their degree floor is a property of the draw rather than of the family

the routing measurement starts every schedule from the identity placement (no placement search), routes the program order as written (no gate reordering) and counts the restore ladder in the mapped depth, with both routers reported; a compiler that searches initial layouts or reorders commuting gates would move these numbers, and no device calibration or error rate is involved

Experiment E's edge set is the specification's, so it measures schedule and verification, not a cheaper preparation: every family emits the same one h per qubit and one cz per edge, and none is a resource advance

the dense-tier ceiling is measured with the policy bound lifted in a separate process and carries no verdict: the referee still answers UNRESOLVED above DENSE_SPEC_LIMIT, and only the price of the arithmetic is new

the ceiling is a property of the declared 8 GiB address-space budget and this host: a larger budget reaches one more width at 16 * 4**n bytes per operator, and the record says which width its wall is at rather than claiming a universal limit
the ceiling measures a non-Clifford GHZ construction; a target with the same number of stabilizers costs the same number of matrix-vector products, but only this construction is measured
tracemalloc peak is the tier's own allocation high-water mark and peak RSS adds the interpreter and NumPy baseline, so a peak reached inside one process cannot be attributed to a single allocation

the third referee decides the unitary, which is a stricter question than the one this package's referees answer: a schedule that permuted its wires would prepare the correct state and fail QCEC, so the comparison is run only on schedules that share one wire order and on constructions that are wrong as operators. A disagreement would mean the two questions came apart on a circuit, and none did

QCEC decided every pair in this corpus, including the 900-qubit one, so the record holds no third-referee abstention: the abstention path exists and is pinned by tests, but this corpus does not exercise it and no claim is made about a pair the tool could not decide

the lookahead window sweep is one host and one process per row; the best window is chosen by mapped depth with the smaller window breaking ties, and depth is not monotone in the window, so no ordering between windows is claimed. The window-8 column reproduces the Experiment D lookahead rows exactly, which is the sweep's own consistency check

the ceiling prices the dense tier as implemented: each stabilizer is materialised as a dense 2**n x 2**n operator, so the wall is 16 * 4**n bytes. Applying the Pauli string as single-qubit gates and index permutations would use O(2**n) memory and move the wall by several qubits; that implementation is not measured here, and none of these numbers is a claim about what the question costs in principle
